scenario.name: Microsoft MSTIC & SANS DFIR — Scheduled Task Creation & TaskCache SD Descriptor Deletion (EventID 4698 / Sysmon EID 12)
scenario.overview: Think of a bright neighborhood pharmacy with a glass prescription drop-off window, rows of labeled medicine bottles on a rotating carousel wall, and a pickup counter bell. At the neighborhood pharmacy drop-off window, a caller slides across a prescription slip whose dosage instructions were subtly rewritten while keeping the doctor’s header. In this real-world scenario, the intruder leaves a hidden spare latch behind so they can walk back into the pharmacy later, then leaves a hidden spare latch behind so they can walk back into the pharmacy later. The head pharmacist reviews the evening dispensing ledger and flags a controlled-cabinet refill that lacks a matching clinic verification signature. In this DFIR walkthrough (MITRE T1053.005 on a compromised Windows server), an adversary registers a SYSTEM scheduled task that launches a payload on a timer, then uses the Tarrask technique to peel the TaskCache index label so schtasks and the Task Scheduler GUI no longer list the job while the engine still runs it. Steps #1 cover lawful task creation logs and on-disk XML, Step #2 covers registry SD deletion and Sysmon alerts, and Step #3 recovers the hidden command line from TaskCache Tasks GUID storage and TaskScheduler run history. Primary detection pivots on pairing Security EventID 4698 with Sysmon registry delete events under TaskCache Tree and hunting GUID-only tasks missing Tree SD values.

stages.title: Stage 1: Scheduled Task Registration & XML Artifact Creation (Security EventID 4698 & TaskScheduler 106)
stages.subtitle: Persistence (T1053.005 - Scheduled Task/Job: Scheduled Task)
stages.description: At the neighborhood pharmacy drop-off window, a caller slides across a prescription slip whose dosage instructions were subtly rewritten while keeping the doctor’s header. Specifically in Step 1, the intruder leaves a hidden spare latch behind so they can walk back into the pharmacy later while everyday visitors and the head pharmacist go about their routine. The attacker executes schtasks.exe /create /tn "\Microsoft\Windows\NetTrace\TelemetrySync" /tr "C:\ProgramData\sync.exe" /sc MINUTE /mo 15 /ru SYSTEM. Windows Security EventID 4698 captures the full embedded TaskContent XML, while svchost.exe writes the XML definition to C:\Windows\System32\Tasks\Microsoft\Windows\NetTrace\TelemetrySync (logged in WinEvent Event 4698 with EventID=4698 , Security / 106 , TaskScheduler/Operational, TaskName=\Microsoft\Windows\NetTrace\TelemetrySync, PrincipalSid=S-1-5-18 , NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM, ExecCommand=C:\ProgramData\sync.exe so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes schtasks.exe /create /tn "\Microsoft\Windows\NetTrace\TelemetrySync" /tr "C:\ProgramData\sync.exe" /sc MINUTE /mo 15 /ru SYSTEM (which Calls the Windows Task Scheduler CLI , schtasks.exe or ITaskService RPC interface to register, modify, or execute a scheduled task XML definition u so that establishes recurring execution persistence , T1053.005 during "Scheduled Task Registration & XML Artifact Creation , Security EventID 4698 & TaskScheduler 106" under SYSTEM or privileged account authority so the implant automatically respawns on schedule, boot, or user logon). Next, the follow-up artifact Security EventID 4698: A scheduled task was created (embeds full <Task> XML) runs (which Calls the Windows Task Scheduler CLI , schtasks.exe or ITaskService RPC interface to register, modify, or execute a scheduled task XML definition u so that establishes recurring execution persistence , T1053.005 during "Scheduled Task Registration & XML Artifact Creation , Security EventID 4698 & TaskScheduler 106" under SYSTEM or privileged account authority so the implant automatically respawns on schedule, boot, or user logon). On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ schtasks.exe /create /tn "\Microsoft\Windows\NetTrace\TelemetrySync" /tr "C:\ProgramData\sync.exe" /sc MINUTE /mo 15 /ru SYSTEM / ⇠#1 ACK 4698) from Node ① (#1 Attacker Admin Session) to Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 TaskCache\Tree SD Registry Key).

stages.title: Stage 2: Tarrask Evasion — Deleting TaskCache\Tree SD Value as SYSTEM (Sysmon EventID 12)
stages.subtitle: Defense Evasion (T1564 - Hide Artifacts: Scheduled Task SD Deletion)
stages.description: Trusting the familiar letterhead, the pharmacy counter rotates the medicine bottle carousel and prepares a restricted bottle without double-checking the original clinic. Here in Step 2 inside the pharmacy, the intruder bypasses the normal inspection rule to reach the prescription bottle carousel wall without disturbing the double-locked controlled cabinet. Following the technique documented by Microsoft MSTIC (Hafnium / Tarrask), the attacker elevates to NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM (to satisfy TrustedInstaller/SYSTEM ACLs on the Schedule key) and deletes the "SD" (Security Descriptor) binary value under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Schedule\TaskCache\Tree\Microsoft\Windows\NetTrace\TelemetrySync and removes the XML file on disk, rendering the task invisible to schtasks /query while keeping it active in TaskCache\Tasks\{GUID} (logged in Sysmon Event 12 with EventID=12 , Sysmon RegistryEvent DeleteValue, TargetObject=HKLM\...\Schedule\TaskCache\Tree\Microsoft\Windows\NetTrace\TelemetrySync\SD, EvasionEffect=Hides task from schtasks.exe /query and Taskschd.msc GUI, ResidualArtifact=HKLM\...\Schedule\TaskCache\Tasks\{GUID}\Actions so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes reg.exe delete "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Schedule\TaskCache\Tree\Microsoft\Windows\NetTrace\TelemetrySync" /v SD /f (which Runs reg.exe delete , or NtDeleteValueKey to strip a specific registry key or security descriptor value , such as the TaskCache\Tree SD value from so that manipulates persistent Windows Registry configuration or credential material , T1564 during "Tarrask Evasion, Deleting TaskCache\Tree SD Value as SYSTEM , Sysmon EventID 12" to establish persistence, alter system behavior, or harvest secrets). Next, the follow-up artifact del /f /q "C:\Windows\System32\Tasks\Microsoft\Windows\NetTrace\TelemetrySync" runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , del /f /q "C:\Windows\System32\Tasks\Microsoft\Windows\NetTrace\TelemetrySync" via System / so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1564 during "Tarrask Evasion, Deleting TaskCache\Tree SD Value as SYSTEM , Sysmon EventID 12" , Following the technique documented by Microsoft MSTIC , Hafnium / Tarrask, the attacker elevates to NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM , to satisfy TrustedInstaller/SYSTEM ACLs on the Schedule key and deletes the "SD" , Security Descriptor binary value under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Schedule\TaskCache\Tree\Microsoft\Windows\NetTrace\TelemetrySync and removes the XML file on disk, rendering the task invisible to schtasks /query while keeping it active in TaskCache\Tasks\{GUID} while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ reg.exe delete "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Schedule\TaskCache\Tree\Microsoft\Windows\NetTrace\TelemetrySync" /v SD /f / ⇠#2 ACK 12) from Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap) to Node ③ (#3 RPC ITaskSchedulerService), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 TaskCache\Tree SD Registry Key).

stages.title: Stage 3: Forensic Recovery from TaskCache\Tasks\{GUID}\Actions & TaskScheduler EventID 200
stages.subtitle: Execution (T1053.005 - TaskCache\Tasks\{GUID} Actions Blob Recovery)
stages.description: Ringing the pickup counter bell, the intruder collects the restricted bottle in an ordinary paper pharmacy bag and steps straight out onto the sidewalk. In this final step inside the pharmacy, the intruder leaves a hidden spare latch behind so they can walk back into the pharmacy later until the pharmacy dispensing ledger catches the mismatch. Even after the SD value and XML file are deleted, the Task Scheduler service continues executing the task every 15 minutes (logging TaskScheduler EventID 200 Action Started) because the binary Actions blob (starting with 0x0300 magic version header) and DynamicInfo timestamps remain intact under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Schedule\TaskCache\Tasks\{GUID} (logged in WinEvent Event 200 with LogChannel=Microsoft-Windows-TaskScheduler/Operational, EventID=200 , Action Executed, TaskRegistryKey=HKLM\...\Schedule\TaskCache\Tasks\{91F0C421-3812-4A99-8231-001122334455}, BinaryActionsBlob=03 00 ... C:\ProgramData\sync.exe , UTF-16LE so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes Get-ItemProperty "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Schedule\TaskCache\Tasks\*" | Select-Object URI, Actions, DynamicInfo (which Calls the Windows Task Scheduler CLI , schtasks.exe or ITaskService RPC interface to register, modify, or execute a scheduled task XML definition u so that establishes recurring execution persistence , T1053.005 during "Forensic Recovery from TaskCache\Tasks\{GUID}\Actions & TaskScheduler EventID 200" under SYSTEM or privileged account authority so the implant automatically respawns on schedule, boot, or user logon). Next, the follow-up artifact TaskScheduler/Operational EventID 200: Task "\Microsoft\Windows\NetTrace\TelemetrySync" launched action "C:\ProgramData\sync.exe" runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , TaskScheduler/Operational EventID 200: Task "\Microsoft\Windows\NetTrace\TelemetrySync" laun so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1053.005 during "Forensic Recovery from TaskCache\Tasks\{GUID}\Actions & TaskScheduler EventID 200" , Even after the SD value and XML file are deleted, the Task Scheduler service continues executing the task every 15 minutes , logging TaskScheduler EventID 200 Action Started because the binary Actions blob , starting with 0x0300 magic version header and DynamicInfo timestamps remain intact under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Schedule\TaskCache\Tasks\{GUID} while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ C:\ProgramData\sync.exe (Launched via hidden TaskCache GUID) / ⇠#3 ACK 200) from Node ③ (#3 RPC ITaskSchedulerService) to Node ④ (#4 svchost.exe (Schedule Service)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 TaskCache\Tree SD Registry Key).
